title: How to give feedback that changes behaviour, not just feelings
performance: Rewrite feedback for an ordinary workplace conversation so the colleague can identify the behaviour being discussed and a relevant next action to try. Success here is clarity of the requested change, not proof of agreement, compliance or later improvement.

assumed_prior: Everyday workplace conversations and the experience of giving or receiving feedback.
No formal feedback framework is assumed.
audience.why: The brief describes corporate employees with everyday conversation experience. Treat them as workplace practitioners who are new to this particular approach, not as novices at work.
audience.motivation: Prepare feedback that is useful without turning a working relationship into a personal judgement. This is the brief's provisional audience assumption, not an interview finding.
audience.context: Ordinary colleague-to-colleague or manager-to-employee feedback. Viewing device, language needs and whether participation is mandatory are unspecified. Design for linear playback with legible captions and optional private drafting; do not assume an interactive player.

strategy.name: worked_example_led
strategy.rationale: The approved sheet offers practical operations, situation, observable behaviour, impact, next action and mutual checks, rather than a survey of frameworks. Demonstrate one concise rewrite, fade its next-action support, then transfer the operations to the viewer's own feedback. Keep the example short for workplace practitioners.
strategy.signature_move: Show the hypothetical wording, revise one part, explain the choice, name the operation, then ask the viewer to use it.

misconceptions.belief: A personality label alone tells the colleague what to change.
misconceptions.why_tempting: A label can feel like a concise summary of a concern. This is a plausible attraction of the source-listed misconception, not a verified belief held by this audience.
misconceptions.evidence_that_breaks_it: F1 and F2 distinguish an action from a person judgement. In the explicitly hypothetical handover, 'careless' does not identify the omitted input or the future action.
misconceptions.replacement: Describe the accurately known workplace action instead of relying on a label.

misconceptions.belief: If the feedback sounds considerate, the recipient will know what to do differently.
misconceptions.why_tempting: Considerate language can seem to solve the relationship concern highlighted in the brief. The attraction is a design rationale, not an audience research finding.
misconceptions.evidence_that_breaks_it: F13 separates tone from actionability. The quiz's considerate revision still leaves the requested handover action unspecified, using F16's lesson criterion.
misconceptions.replacement: Keep a considerate tone and specify a relevant future action; evaluate each separately.

misconceptions.belief: A clear rewrite, or a recipient repeating it back, proves that behaviour will change.
misconceptions.why_tempting: Resolving ambiguity can feel like resolving the whole workplace problem. This is a plausible attraction, not an established audience belief.
misconceptions.evidence_that_breaks_it: F11 limits the check to clarity; F14 rejects guaranteed change from wording alone. F8 identifies resources and authority as constraints to discuss.
misconceptions.replacement: Check clarity, discuss feasibility and arrange an appropriate opportunity to review; do not promise compliance.

hook.sketch: Imagine a handover omitted a missing client file, and you had to move a review. You say, 'Please be more thoughtful'; your colleague looks uneasy and asks, 'What should I do differently?'
hook.framing: This entire workplace scene, its dialogue and its emotional reaction are invented for teaching. Introduce it with 'Imagine', never as a testimonial or an observed result.

arc.promise: By the end, you can revise feedback you need to give so the colleague can identify the behaviour and a next action to discuss.
arc.bridge_from_prior: Recall an ordinary feedback conversation: you can notice a reaction without knowing whether the recipient has understood the requested change. In the imagined handover, acknowledge the uneasy response, then ask what work action still needs to be made clear. Feelings can affect engagement; they are not the actionability test.

running_example.context: Imagine that during a project handover, a colleague omitted that a client file needed for a draft was missing. You booked a review and later had to move it. Assume the missing-input information was available to the colleague; whether sharing it earlier is feasible remains a discussion, not a conclusion.
running_example.initial_draft: You're careless. Please be more thoughtful about handovers.
running_example.situation_behaviour_impact_revision: At the handover for the draft, your update did not mention the missing client file. I booked a review and then had to move it.
running_example.next_action_revision: At the next handover, could you flag any missing input before I book the review?
running_example.perspective_prompt: What was happening from your side?
running_example.feasibility_prompt: Would you have that information at the handover, and could you flag it then? What would get in the way?
running_example.mutual_check_prompt: I want to check that I explained this clearly: how would you describe the issue, and what would you do differently at the next handover?
running_example.use_limit: These are sample lines for the invented case, not a universal script. Present the actual behaviour and impact as accurately known only within this imagined scene. Do not import its details into the viewer's own feedback.

sections.title: A reaction is not yet a next action
sections.goal: the viewer can explain why a considerate response and an identifiable next action are separate tests of feedback.
sections.recap: Care about the reaction, and make the requested change clear.
teaching_beats: Deliver the hook and promise inside this section, with no agenda slide or framework name first.
Use the same handover scene for the bridge from prior conversations. Do not generalise the imagined uneasy reaction into a prediction about recipients.
Reveal concrete anchors before terminology: what happened in the handover, then what could happen differently next time. Name these anchors behaviour and next action.
Distinguish the relationship concern from the actionability question without suggesting that either cancels the other.
sections.learner_job: Privately recall feedback that sounded considerate but left you uncertain about the requested action. No stop or disclosure required.
sections.screen_change: The initial feedback bubble appears; an imagined question bubble replaces a generic reaction marker. Highlight the unanswered 'do differently' phrase, not exaggerated facial acting.
sections.delivery_notes: Open with a curious question, acknowledge the relationship concern warmly, and state the promise directly.

sections.title: Describe the event, not the person
sections.goal: the viewer can use the approach to replace a person judgement with a situation, observable behaviour and relevant impact.
sections.recap: Locate the event, describe the action, explain the relevant impact.
teaching_beats: Show the imagined draft, 'You're careless', and fairly acknowledge its appeal as shorthand. Ask which workplace action the label identifies; it does not identify one on its own.
Replace the label with 'At the handover for the draft'; name situation only after the concrete revision appears.
Add 'your update did not mention the missing client file'; name observable behaviour. Do not add 'you did not care' or infer intent.
Add 'I booked a review and then had to move it'; name impact. In this fictional case the work consequence is stipulated, not independently evidenced.
Give the rationale with F3's qualification: directing attention to the task is generally more favourable to performance, but effects vary and improvement is not guaranteed.

Make the evidence boundary usable: use accurate details, identify secondhand information, and separate interpretation or reported experience from established consequences. A behaviour description may still be disputed.
sections.learner_job: Notice which part of your own draft is an action and which is a person label or inferred motive. Do not stop playback.
sections.screen_change: Replace the label in the same feedback card with event-specific text. Reveal the situation, behaviour and impact labels beside their clauses, one at a time.
sections.delivery_notes: Keep the worked example brisk. Slow only enough to distinguish an observed action from an inferred motive; avoid a long research aside.

sections.title: Make an action discussable
sections.goal: the viewer can apply a specific next-action proposal and mutual checks to the hypothetical handover feedback.
sections.recap: Propose a doable action, hear their account, and check what your words made clear.
teaching_beats: Complete the handover example with the next-action revision. Contrast this concrete request with the earlier 'be more thoughtful', without launching a second scenario.
Explain that the proposed action must fit the task and the colleague's responsibilities. Invite their account before treating your interpretation as settled.

Show the perspective and feasibility prompts from arc.running_example. If the assumed access to missing-input information is wrong, revise the request or help address the obstacle rather than demand more effort.
Insert a brief visual consolidation after these prompts before introducing the mutual check. Keep the assembled feedback card visible with no new terminology during that beat.
Demonstrate the mutual-check prompt as a check on your explanation, not a test of the colleague's intelligence. Ask both what behaviour was discussed and what they would do differently.
State that these proposed checks are practical, not validated measures. A clear answer does not establish agreement, ability or compliance, and wording alone does not guarantee change.

Generalise the assembled example as this lesson's practical approach, combining Situation-Behavior-Impact guidance with next-action discussion and proposed checks. It is not a separately validated package or mandatory script.
sections.learner_job: Mentally finish 'At the next handover...' with a visible action before the narrator demonstrates the complete proposal. This is a continuous teaching prompt, not a prediction pause.
sections.screen_change: Append the future-action clause to the existing card. Reveal perspective and feasibility bubbles in sequence; simplify back to the card; then reveal the mutual-check bubble. No successful-performance montage.
sections.delivery_notes: Slow on the shift from 'be more thoughtful' to the specific action. Treat the check as mutual clarification, never as a challenge to the recipient.

sections.title: Strip the rewrite down to its essentials
sections.goal: the viewer can distinguish the behaviour being discussed from the future action requested in the running example.
teaching_beats: Remove the dialogue and most annotations. Show only the handover's behaviour clause and an empty next-action slot.
Invite the viewer to supply the missing next-action clause mentally; keep playback continuous, then restore the worked clause.
Name the difference between the past action being discussed and the future action being requested.
Recall that describing a next action makes the request clear; it is not evidence that the colleague accepts it.
sections.learner_job: Complete the missing clause without the operation labels, then compare your wording to the restored example.
sections.screen_change: The dense dialogue card reduces to two short lines. The next-action line clears, then refills; there is no new setting or character business.
sections.delivery_notes: Leave conversational space between the two clauses. Use fewer words and a calm recap, not additional concepts.

sections.title: Choose by actionability, not just politeness
sections.goal: the viewer can judge which revision makes a relevant future handover action identifiable.
sections.recap: Prefer the revision that identifies a relevant next action, and keep the tone considerate.
teaching_beats: Run pacing.recall_moments.q1 after s4 using the shared situation, behaviour and impact stem. Offer exactly the specified options.
Keep the answer hidden until after the silent pause. Reveal only the correct option and explain the single tempting wrong belief.
The correct option identifies an action and when it matters. The wrong option may sound considerate but does not state what to do differently.
Finish by distinguishing clarity from feasibility and agreement; the chosen request still needs discussion in the real conversation.
Say this is the lesson's practical criterion, not a validated assessment instrument.
sections.learner_job: Choose the revision by the action the recipient could identify, not the warmer-sounding sentence.
sections.screen_change: Present a common context stem and two revision cards. After the pause, highlight the next-action phrase in the correct card; retain only a short 'kind but unspecified' note for the other card.
sections.delivery_notes: Read and address the options in displayed order without signalling the answer. After the pause, explain one wrong belief only.

sections.title: Rewrite feedback you actually need to give
sections.goal: the viewer can draft feedback that specifies an accurately described behaviour and a relevant next action, with prompts to discuss perspective, feasibility and understanding.
sections.recap: Draft an accurate account and a specific request, then leave room to discuss it.
teaching_beats: Before drafting, establish the boundary: choose an ordinary workplace feedback issue, not a safety, misconduct or disciplinary matter. Those require the organisation's relevant process or appropriate advice.
Move from the handover example to the viewer's own work without adding another invented case. Use transfer_tasks.t1 as the independent task.
Recall the operations first without displaying their names; then reveal the writing scaffold in short groups.

Have the viewer begin by replacing a person label with an accurate behaviour description and drafting the next-action line. Present situation and impact as supporting context, not as permission to invent precision.
Ask them to note what they need to verify and what the colleague needs to clarify. Include perspective, feasible resources and authority, and a mutual-check prompt.
Use the self-review criteria in transfer_tasks.t1. Provide no model answer for the viewer's unknown event.
Invite completion and fuller review after playback; do not require a second in-video stopping check or imply that a finished workplace draft has been independently assessed.
sections.learner_job: Begin a private rewrite of an actual feedback issue. If no appropriate issue is available, draft another wording of the same hypothetical handover example and mark it as hypothetical.
sections.screen_change: Keep a small handover anchor while revealing a blank, neutral writing scaffold. Labels appear only beside the fields being discussed, not as a full screen of bullets.
sections.delivery_notes: Use a capable-colleague tone. Give a concrete starting instruction, allow ordinary narration gaps, and make the optional after-video completion explicit.

sections.title: Resolve the ambiguity, not the whole future
sections.goal: the viewer can justify whether the revised feedback makes the requested change clear without treating clarity as proof of future behaviour change.
teaching_beats: Return to the opening handover and show the revised feedback with its next-action clause.
Frame any recipient response with 'In this imagined conversation, say the colleague answers...' before the example response in arc.payoff.
Identify exactly what the response establishes: the behaviour and next action are now identifiable. Do not call it an agreement or depict the action already succeeding.
Suggest a later opportunity to review whether an agreed action helped the work and adjust it as needed. Do not invent a review date or make follow-up universal.
Close with the viewer's own draft and the pocket rule from transfer_tasks.t1, not with a promise that wording will make people change.
sections.learner_job: Use the pocket rule to check your draft: could the colleague name the behaviour and what to try next? Keep any unresolved fact or feasibility question visible.
sections.screen_change: The opening feedback bubble is replaced with the revised clauses. A hypothetical response names the next action; end on the compact pocket rule, with no celebratory compliance scene.
sections.delivery_notes: Settle the pace. Resolve the opening question plainly, then give the clarity-versus-change limit equal vocal weight.

payoff.return_to_hook: In the imagined handover conversation, the revised wording identifies the omitted missing-input information, its work impact and a request to flag missing inputs before the next review is booked.
payoff.hypothetical_recipient_response: In this imagined conversation, say the colleague answers: 'The issue was not mentioning the missing client file in the handover. The action you're asking about is flagging missing inputs before you book the review.'
payoff.what_is_resolved: The colleague can identify the behaviour and the proposed next action, answering 'What should I do differently?' from the hook.
payoff.what_is_not_resolved: The reply does not establish agreement, ability, future compliance or improved work. The colleague's perspective, constraints and feelings still matter.
payoff.closing_line: Before you give the feedback, check your draft: can they name the behaviour and what to try next?

practice_ladder.support: Show the complete hypothetical rewrite incrementally, with each operation named after its concrete clause. Demonstrate the conversation prompts and qualified limits.
practice_ladder.learner_action: Track how the label becomes an account of behaviour and how the vague request becomes a future action.
practice_ladder.success_criteria: The example identifies a specific situation, an action rather than a motive, an accurately stipulated impact and a relevant proposed next action.

practice_ladder.support: Retain the same situation, behaviour and impact, but remove the next-action clause and labels. Restore the clause during continuous narration.
practice_ladder.learner_action: Mentally complete the future-action clause, then distinguish it from the behaviour clause.
practice_ladder.success_criteria: The completion names a relevant action at a future handover, rather than a personality change or a general wish.

practice_ladder.support: Provide the common stem and two revisions, with no answer until after the pause.
practice_ladder.learner_action: Choose the actionable revision and explain the criterion.
practice_ladder.success_criteria: Choose B because it identifies an action in the relevant future context, not merely because of its tone.
practice_ladder.feedback: Use pacing.recall_moments.q1.answer and its single tempting_wrong explanation.

practice_ladder.support: Provide an unfilled scaffold and self-review criteria, but no invented facts or model answer for the learner's workplace event.
practice_ladder.learner_action: Begin a private draft, note uncertainties, and complete transfer_tasks.t1 after playback.
practice_ladder.success_criteria: A reader could identify the described behaviour and a relevant proposed next action; evidence, interpretation and feasibility are not falsely presented as settled.
practice_ladder.feedback: Self-review against transfer_tasks.t1.criteria. A real colleague's mutual clarity check can later inform revision; no validated score or independent assessment is claimed.

pacing.duration_basis: Provisional editorial runtime because no requested length was supplied. Section allocations include hook, promise, practice, silent pause and payoff.
pacing.spoken_word_budget_note: Allow approximately 1100 spoken words, an editorial estimate excluding the quiz's silent pause. Do not fill pauses with narration to hit a word count.

slowdown_at.moment: Replace 'be more thoughtful' with the specific next-handover action, then distinguish a clear request from feasible or agreed action.
slowdown_at.reason: This is the central shift the learner must reproduce, and a plausible place to mistake clarity for guaranteed change.

recall_moments.prompt: What did we describe instead of the personality label? Now add what the colleague could try at the next handover.
recall_moments.expected_retrieval: The specific handover behaviour, not the judgement 'careless'.
recall_moments.screen_support: Highlight the existing behaviour clause; keep playback continuous.

recall_moments.prompt: Both revisions follow this account: 'At the handover for the draft, your update did not mention the missing client file. I booked a review and then had to move it.' Which ending makes a relevant future action identifiable?

options.text: Please be more thoughtful at handovers; I know you mean well.
At the next handover, could you flag any missing input before I book the review?

answer.text: B identifies the next action: flag missing inputs before the review is booked.
answer.explanation: It states what to do and the relevant future situation. The action still needs a perspective and feasibility discussion; selecting it proves neither agreement nor future behaviour change.

tempting_wrong.belief: Considerate wording means the recipient knows what to do differently.
tempting_wrong.why_tempting: A sounds reassuring and addresses the relationship concern.
tempting_wrong.why_wrong: It leaves 'more thoughtful' unspecified and does not identify a next action. Its assertion about intent also goes beyond the stated behaviour.

build.question_scene: Show the common stem and both options with no answer marker. Address A then B. End narration with 'pause the video and decide'.
build.answer_scene: Reveal B in the next scene. Highlight 'flag any missing input' and the booking context. Explain A's single tempting belief, then state the clarity limit.
build.answer_takeaway_on_screen: Specific action, not just considerate wording.
build.allocation_note: Reserve the stopping check and explanation within s5's duration. Do not speak additional wrong options or add another takeaway the screen cannot carry.

recall_moments.prompt: Before the scaffold appears, recall what your colleague needs to identify: the behaviour and what to try next. What else do you need to discuss rather than assume?
recall_moments.expected_retrieval: Perspective, feasibility and a mutual check of what the explanation made clear.
recall_moments.screen_support: Show only the short behaviour and next-action anchors initially; reveal the scaffold afterwards.

recall_moments.prompt: If they can name the action, what have you checked, and what have you not proved?
recall_moments.expected_retrieval: You checked clarity, not agreement, ability or future compliance.
recall_moments.screen_support: Highlight the hypothetical response, then the short clarity-limit caption.

pacing.participation_note: Use continuous mental-completion and recall prompts between the worked example and quiz. Independent drafting may begin during s6 and be completed after playback. Do not add unplanned quizzes or prediction pauses.

transfer_tasks.task: Choose ordinary feedback you need to give. Replace any person judgement with an accurate description of the behaviour; locate its situation, explain the relevant impact, and draft a specific future action to discuss. Add prompts for the colleague's account, feasibility and a mutual understanding check. Begin during playback and complete privately afterwards.
scaffold: Situation: where or when did this occur, using details I can describe accurately?
Behaviour: what action happened, and how do I know?
Impact: what relevant work consequence or personal experience can I accurately report? What is only my interpretation?
Next action: what could the colleague try in a relevant future situation?
Conversation: what do I need to hear from them, and what resources or authority could constrain the request?
Mutual check: how would they describe the issue and what they would do differently?
criteria: The draft is about an ordinary work issue within the lesson's scope.
A colleague could identify the behaviour without having to translate a personality label or inferred motive.
The account does not invent precision, hide secondhand information or present interpretation as established consequence.
The next action fits the behaviour, work context and colleague's responsibilities; it is not merely 'be better' or 'be thoughtful'.
The draft makes room for the colleague's perspective and constraints, and checks the giver's explanation respectfully.
The tone remains considerate, while actionability is judged separately.
Unresolved facts, feasibility and agreement remain open rather than being written as settled.
transfer_tasks.self_review: Read the draft as the recipient and state the behaviour and next action in your own words. If either is unclear, revise it. This is a lesson self-check, not a validated assessment.
transfer_tasks.use_at_work: In an appropriate real conversation, invite the colleague's account and discuss what is feasible before assuming the proposal is settled. Use the mutual check as clarification. If an action is agreed, consider a later opportunity to review whether it helped and adjust.
transfer_tasks.scope_boundary: For safety, misconduct or disciplinary matters, check the required organisational process or seek appropriate advice rather than substituting this approach.
transfer_tasks.pocket_rule: Name the behaviour. Discuss what to try next. Check what is clear.

gagne.attention: arc.hook and arc.sections[s1].screen_change establish the unresolved hypothetical question.
gagne.objective: arc.promise states the practical rewrite outcome inside s1.
gagne.recall_prior: arc.bridge_from_prior and arc.sections[s1].learner_job connect to everyday feedback conversations.
gagne.present: arc.sections[s2].teaching_beats and arc.sections[s3].teaching_beats demonstrate the practical approach in one running example.
gagne.guidance: strategy.signature_move, arc.running_example and practice_ladder[worked] show the operations and their caveats.
gagne.practice: practice_ladder[faded], pacing.recall_moments[q1] and transfer_tasks[t1] elicit completion, judgement and drafting.
gagne.feedback: pacing.recall_moments[q1].answer and .tempting_wrong explain the choice; transfer_tasks[t1].criteria support private revision.
gagne.assess: pacing.recall_moments[q1] assesses actionability discrimination; transfer_tasks[t1].self_review checks the final draft against explicit criteria. Neither is a validated instrument or independently scored performance test.
gagne.transfer: arc.payoff, pacing.recall_moments[r3] and transfer_tasks[t1].use_at_work return to the dilemma and the viewer's own work.

merrill.problem_centred: arc.running_example presents one unresolved handover conversation; transfer_tasks[t1] targets an actual feedback need.
merrill.activation: arc.bridge_from_prior and arc.sections[s1].learner_job activate existing workplace-conversation experience.
merrill.demonstration: arc.sections[s2] and arc.sections[s3], with practice_ladder[worked], construct the complete rewrite and mutual-check prompts.
merrill.application: practice_ladder[faded], pacing.recall_moments[q1] and arc.sections[s6].learner_job require completion, decision and initial drafting.
merrill.integration: transfer_tasks[t1].use_at_work and arc.sections[s7] connect the private draft to a real conversation and an appropriate review opportunity.

mayer.coherence: arc.running_example.use_limit and arc.sections[].screen_change keep the same handover setting; omit unrelated office business, decorative motion and success montages.
mayer.signalling: arc.sections[s2].screen_change pairs each newly named operation with its clause; pacing.slowdown_at singles out the next-action shift in s3.
mayer.redundancy: Use short operation labels and the necessary example wording, not slide transcripts of explanations. Requested captions remain available as captions rather than duplicated paragraph graphics.
mayer.contiguity: arc.sections[s2].screen_change places labels beside their clauses as the narrator addresses them; s3's prompts appear with their corresponding dialogue.
mayer.segmenting: s2 introduces the account before s3 introduces the conversation; s3 includes a visual consolidation before mutual checks; s4 is a real low-density rest.
mayer.pre_training: s1 reveals the concrete behaviour and next-action anchors before naming them. s2 names situation, behaviour and impact as each concrete part is built, before s3 runs the assembled conversation. Do not front-load a terminology agenda.

arcs.attention: arc.hook asks a concrete, unresolved question without defining feedback terms.
arcs.relevance: arc.promise and transfer_tasks[t1] connect immediately to feedback the viewer needs to give.
arcs.confidence: practice_ladder progresses from a concise worked rewrite to a missing clause, a criteria-based choice and an independent draft.
arcs.satisfaction: arc.payoff resolves the opening ambiguity and transfer_tasks[t1].pocket_rule provides a usable final check, without claiming later compliance.

framework_audit.bloom_path: understand -> apply -> apply -> analyze -> evaluate -> create -> evaluate

delivery_contract.persona: Requested woman presenter as a warm mentor and capable colleague. This choice does not imply character acting or a particular visual performance.
delivery_contract.narration: Use direct second-person language. Explain displayed operations rather than reciting captions. Whenever a set is displayed, address every item in displayed order; reveal long scaffolds in groups to make that possible.
delivery_contract.visual_default: Proposed classic flat story-cartoon illustration, restrained adult workplace tone, one recurring handover setting, concise anchors and legible captions.
delivery_contract.alternatives_preserved: A more dimensional or performed treatment remains an option, not a silent substitution. Plain versus cinematic storytelling, illustrated faces and character acting remain unselected.
delivery_contract.motion_rule: Use motion only to replace vague wording, reveal the current clause, simplify the comparison, or reveal the quiz answer. Section screen_change fields specify the informational change; no acting is required.

grounding.approved_material: All instructional claims and assessment criteria derive from the supplied approved knowledge sheet, F1 to F18. Fictional workplace details and sample dialogue are explicitly framed as imagined.
grounding.method_status: Practical synthesis of Situation-Behavior-Impact guidance, goal-setting principles and proposed comprehension checks. Do not call it an independently validated intervention or universal script.
not_verified: Named research references have not been retrieved or independently checked in this session.
The supplied sheet states that the skeptic marked facts unverifiable and human review is required before scripting.
The audience assumptions have not been tested by interview.
The intended peer-versus-manager emphasis, runtime and viewing context are unspecified.
Organisation-specific policies, actual workplace events, proposed actions and later behaviour outcomes have not been verified.

flags: DURATION-MISMATCH: No requested length was supplied. The 480-second runtime is a provisional editorial allocation, not a confirmed requirement; confirm before scripting.

HUMAN-REVIEW-REQUIRED: The supplied approval note requires human review before scripting. Named references were not independently checked, and this plan preserves the sheet's qualifications rather than claiming verification.
CONTEXT-OPEN: Peer-to-peer versus manager-to-employee emphasis is unspecified. The plan remains within the sheet's ordinary-feedback scope and assumes no authority to compel compliance.
POLICY-NOT-VERIFIED: Organisation-specific safety, misconduct and disciplinary requirements have not been supplied or checked. Keep the scope boundary explicit.

PRESENTATION-OPEN: Preserve story-cartoon, captions and the woman mentor presenter. Classic flat illustration is a proposed default; plain versus cinematic treatment and character acting remain unselected.
VIEWING-CONTEXT-OPEN: Device, language needs and delivery setting are unknown. Confirm them before finalising text sizes and caption production.
